bodies.thread:
Table-aware ingestion decreased recall@5 from 0.733 to 0.667. We rejected it because the data proved it hurt performance, even though it seemed like a good idea.

Most RAG projects skip the hard work of building a golden-question eval harness. Without objective, numerical proof, you are just guessing if your retrieval actually works.

My naive retrieval pipeline only hit a recall@5 of 0.367. Structure-aware chunking pushed that to 0.467, and hybrid retrieval brought it up to 0.733.

The corpus contains 1,971 / 2,144 (92%) chunks with a 16+ character all-lowercase weld. These welded tokens hide data from keyword search and break retrieval.

Increasing the evaluation set from 30 to 60 questions was necessary. It stopped us from chasing the wrong levers and revealed that 45% of failures were never-retrieved chunks.

A RAG system should be evaluated using a golden-question harness that provides objective, numerical proof of retrieval quality rather than relying on qualitative assessment.
